title: Supercurrent detection and manipulation of topological phase transitions in Shiba-Majorana hybrid systems
authors: Debika Debnath, Ioannis Ioannidis, Paramita Dutta, Mircea Trif, Thore Posske
abstract: The non-Abelian statistics of Majorana zero modes has inspired numerous proposals for their detection and manipulation in topological superconductors. Implementations based on magnetic adatoms deposited on superconductors draw particular attention due to their capabilities for precise atomic manipulation and the control over disorder. Here, we propose a scheme for detecting changes in the ground state parity of a topologically non-trivial adatom system by passing supercurrent through their low-energy modes. We unravel characteristic discontinuities in the critical current driven by zero-energy level crossings. We apply these findings to a setup where the Majorana coupling is mediated by a single control magnetic adatom hosting a Yu-Shiba-Rusinov state, and test the robustness of our results against finite temperatures and different tunneling regimes. Our findings introduce a non-invasive approach for reading out and controlling the ground state parity of Majorana states in Shiba-Majorana hybrid systems.
summary: This work proposes using the supercurrent flowing through Shiba-Majorana hybrid systems to detect topological phase transitions. By analyzing characteristic discontinuities in the critical supercurrent, the authors introduce a non-invasive method to read out and control the ground state parity of Majorana zero modes. This advances the field by linking measurable transport properties to abstract topological quantum states.
main_problem: The paper addresses the detection and manipulation of topological phase transitions occurring in Shiba-Majorana hybrid superconducting systems.
main_result: Supercurrent discontinuities observed when passing supercurrent through the system provide a non-invasive method to read out and control the ground state parity of Majorana states.
method: The authors utilize theoretical modeling based on the supercurrent calculation derived from the ground state energy, $I(\phi) = 2\partial E_{GS}(\phi) / \partial \phi$.
model_or_system: The system involves Shiba-Majorana hybrid structures, modeled by an effective Hamiltonian $H_{eff}$ coupling a superconducting STM tip to low-energy Shiba-Majorana modes mediated by a control magnetic adatom.
key_observables: Supercurrent $I(\phi)$ as a function of superconducting phase bias $\phi$, and characteristic discontinuities in the critical current $I_c$.
important_parameters: Superconducting phase bias $\phi$, finite temperature $T$, and the relative energy scales of the Shiba and Majorana couplings ($|\epsilon_M|$ vs $|\epsilon_S|$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the system follows the lowest-energy branch and focuses on the contribution of discrete in-gap states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup involving adatom chains and the supercurrent jump coinciding with the sign change of the inner Majoranas hybridization energy, and show the effect of finite temperature smearing on the transition signature.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by projecting the Hamiltonian onto the low-energy subspace, deriving the supercurrent dependence on the phase bias, and then analyzing the resulting discontinuities as signatures of topological phase transitions.
why_interesting: The use of supercurrent measurements as a diagnostic tool for topological transitions bridges superconducting transport measurements with fundamental topological physics, which is relevant for understanding quantum state readout in superconducting circuits.
